claim: President Biden said he inherited 9% inflation when he took office.
ground_truth_notes: Year-over-year inflation was about 1.4% when Biden was inaugurated in January 2021. It took about a year and a half to reach 9%, in June 2022.
notes: Tests whether the system catches a claim asserting a value at the wrong point in time — exactly the temporal-mismatch guard built into the confidence scorer.

claim: Inflation is at a 40-year high, and rates have been climbing throughout Biden's time in office.
ground_truth_notes: The 40-year-high figure was accurate at time of the claim, but inflation had already been climbing before Biden took office — the claim implies the rise started on his watch.
notes: Correct number, wrong causal attribution/baseline — the exact 'true number, misleading framing' pattern from PLAN.md.

claim: The national debt was about $27.8 trillion when Biden took office and is around $34.4 trillion now.
ground_truth_notes: PolitiFact reports the debt at roughly $27.8T at Biden's inauguration (Jan 2021) and roughly $34.4T as of early 2024.
notes: Clean quantitative baseline case — directly answerable via the Treasury source with no framing trap. Should be a 'should always get this right' case.

claim: We now have historic low unemployment in America among all groups of people.
ground_truth_notes: Unemployment was low by historical standards, but the claim used present tense ('now') while the rate had trended upward for roughly two years and was 0.6-2 points above the record low for each group at time of the claim.
notes: Present-tense claim about a trailing trend — tests whether the system notices the direction of travel, not just the latest single value.

claim: West Virginia's unemployment rate hit a record low under Governor Jim Justice.
ground_truth_notes: West Virginia's unemployment rate hit 2.4% in April/May 2023, beating the prior record of 2.5% set the month before.
notes: Deliberately marked expected_coverage=no: the BLS client only carries NATIONAL series (LNS*), not state-level unemployment. This is a genuine, currently-unaddressed coverage gap this claim is meant to surface, not a system bug being tested for a pass/fail.

claim: President Trump says the US has 'no inflation.'
ground_truth_notes: By two standard measures (CPI, PCE), inflation was not zero at the time of the claim.
notes: Absolute claim ('no inflation') that should be straightforwardly contradicted by any nonzero CPI reading.

claim: One-fourth of the U.S. national debt was accumulated under Donald Trump.
ground_truth_notes: PolitiFact rated this accurate, though much of the debt growth reflects mandatory spending (Social Security, Medicare) rather than discretionary policy choices.
notes: Requires a multi-point-in-time comparison (debt at two different dates), which is a harder multi-hop query than a single-point lookup. Marked 'partial' coverage since Treasury has the raw data but the system has no built-in delta/comparison-across-years reasoning.

claim: The federal deficit has fallen under Biden.
ground_truth_notes: The deficit did fall, but mostly because pandemic-era spending wound down, not due to new deficit-reduction policy — and a smaller deficit still means the debt keeps growing, just more slowly. The claim's implication (debt is being paid down) is false.
notes: Deliberately marked expected_coverage=no: there is no dedicated annual-deficit source wired up (Treasury only covers total debt outstanding, not the deficit calculation). Also a deficit-vs-debt conceptual trap — a system that conflates the two would get this wrong even with the right raw numbers.

claim: Violent crime is near a record 50-year low.
ground_truth_notes: Violent crime peaked in the early 1990s and, per preliminary 2023 estimates, was near/at a 50-year low.
notes: No crime data source is wired up (FBI UCR/NIBRS explicitly out of scope per the 2026-07-20 pivot). This claim exists purely to test coverage honesty: does the system say 'I don't have a source for this' instead of guessing?

claim: Violent crime rose 43% under the Biden-Harris administration.
ground_truth_notes: One federal survey (NCVS) shows a 43% rise 2020-2022, but that figure omits 2023-2024, and FBI data over the same window shows violent crime falling, not rising. Rated Mostly False by PolitiFact.
notes: Double trap: no crime source AND a real number pulled from a cherry-picked source/timeframe. Tests coverage honesty and framing awareness simultaneously.

claim: 8 million migrants have come in under Biden.
ground_truth_notes: PolitiFact rated the closely related claim ('Biden let in 8 million people') Mostly False — border encounters (events, not people) reached roughly 8 million, but only about 2.3 million people were actually released into the U.S.
notes: No CBP/DHS source is wired up. Also a units trap: conflates 'encounters' (events) with 'people' — a real, common misinformation pattern in this domain.

claim: There have been over 4.6 million encounters at the southern border, and most of those people have been released into the interior and will stay indefinitely.
ground_truth_notes: Rated Half True: the encounter figure was roughly accurate, but about 53% of encounters resulted in expulsion, not release — 'most... will stay indefinitely' overstates the outcome.
notes: Correct headline number, wrong conclusion drawn from it — another instance of the framing-trap pattern, in an uncovered domain.

claim: There have been over 150,000 illegal border crossings per month for 16 consecutive months.
ground_truth_notes: Rated Mostly True on the raw figure, but the data tracks encounter events, not unique people — the same person crossing multiple times counts multiple times, so it overstates the number of distinct individuals.
notes: Same events-vs-people trap as immig-001, different administration/timeframe.
